adminGuide.title: How AI, RAG, and MCP work
adminGuide.description: An operational guide to the assistant, external search, synchronization, and MCP security boundaries.
adminGuide.assistantDescription: The built-in assistant runs private, page-bound chats through the provider configured for each space. Its space settings show request and token usage for today and the last 7 calendar days. Agent mode can call approved Docmost tools and applies page changes only after the initiating user confirms them.
adminGuide.retrievalDescription: Space search runs while an answer is generated. It asks an external index for candidates, then Docmost rechecks every source against the database, current access rules, and AI exclusions. Retrieval failure does not fail the chat.
adminGuide.ragDescription: The read-only /api/rag/* API exports full and incremental content feeds to an external indexer. It does not perform search or answer questions, and every RAG key is restricted to one space.
adminGuide.inboundMcpDescription: External assistants connect to Docmost at the root /mcp endpoint with a scoped MCP key. The endpoint is stateless and exposes only read tools allowed by the key's exact capability policy.
adminGuide.outboundMcpDescription: The Docmost Agent can call tools on approved remote MCP servers. This is the opposite direction from inbound MCP and uses separate settings and credentials.
adminGuide.setupDescription: Open the relevant settings area. Deployment environment allowlists and kill switches remain operator-managed.
adminGuide.syncDescription: Docmost has no local embedding table. Built-in RAG synchronization runs inside the main Docmost process, uses shared Redis for coordination, and stores one encrypted Open WebUI writer key per space in PostgreSQL. Configure the Open WebUI origin, Knowledge Base ID, and writer key in the space RAG synchronization tab. Enable the deployment with RAG_SYNC_ENABLED and allow the exact origin through RAG_SYNC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. The index includes every page allowed by the space AI policy; direct Open WebUI access can therefore expose content beyond a user's Docmost ACL. Query and writer credentials remain separate.
adminGuide.syncStepDelta: Each feed uses an opaque cursor bound to one fixed database snapshot. Keep its starting watermark until hasMore=false; only the terminal page advances the checkpoint, and retries must remain idempotent.
adminGuide.riskTiming: Freshness is the polling interval plus cycle processing time. A longer interval increases staleness; a very short interval raises Docmost, Redis, and Open WebUI load and can cause 429/503 responses.
adminGuide.riskDelivery: Feeds are at least once. Lease or slot loss aborts the current remote request and prevents new work; reconciliation handles a side effect that completed before cancellation reached the remote service.
adminGuide.riskModel: Changing the embedding model or chunking in the external index does not change Docmost content hashes. RAG Sync skips unchanged sources, so perform the external platform's supported full rebuild when its indexing model changes.
adminGuide.securitySourceAccess: Docmost rechecks live source state, exclusions, and ACL before and during generation, when reusing chat history, and before returning editor-selection results. Page attachments and private chat files are guarded too, and selected text remains untrusted input. If access changes, partial text, reasoning, and citations are cleared and the message becomes restricted.
adminGuide.securityInbound: Inbound /mcp and /api/rag/* accept only their own key types; user sessions and the other key type are rejected. Keys remain bounded by their creator's current space access and page visibility. The token is returned only at creation; its type, space, creator, and expiry cannot be updated.
adminGuide.securityOutbound: Outbound MCP is closed unless the deployment switch, workspace switch, enabled server, space binding, group policy, and user opt-in all allow it. The deployment kill switch is AI_EXTERNAL_MCP_ENABLED.
adminGuide.securityOutboundGroups: Space administrators manage group rules on each server binding. A deny rule wins; otherwise a selected group tool list narrows the workspace and space allowlists by intersection.
adminGuide.securitySecrets: Provider, retrieval, Open WebUI writer, RAG, inbound MCP, and outbound MCP credentials are separate secrets. Keep per-space credential values out of Docker environment and metadata, logs, and URLs. Before rotating APP_SECRET, disable every RAG sync binding and wait for cleanup; the secret also signs remote ownership metadata. If it was rotated too early, restore the previous value before cleanup, then re-enter encrypted credentials.
adminGuide.securityRemote: Outbound MCP sends selected Docmost data to another system. Remote descriptions, schemas, and results are untrusted; 'read-only' is Docmost's policy classification, not proof that the remote implementation has no side effects.
adminGuide.operationsSetup: Configure and test the model and optional retrieval for every space. Approve deployment origins first, keep search disabled until an adapter is ready, and use the built-in and external tool policies to narrow access.
adminGuide.operationsProfileNames: Keep assistant profile names unique within each space. A duplicate returns 409 with ai_profile_name_conflict; reload the list if needed and choose another name.
adminGuide.operationsRagMigration: When replacing the standalone RAG worker, stop it first, migrate with RAG_SYNC_ENABLED=false, then configure, Test, and Enable each space. Old environment secrets are not imported. Roll back with the deployment switch, not migration down.
adminGuide.operationsRecovery: On failure, recover dependencies before retrying, keep PostgreSQL authoritative, and preserve the Knowledge Base during mapping recovery. For an emergency RAG Sync rollback, set RAG_SYNC_ENABLED=false and restart Docmost; AI_EXTERNAL_MCP_ENABLED controls only outbound MCP.
adminGuide.templateExportScope: Template catalog entries are excluded. Pages created from templates are exported as ordinary materialized pages.

commandPrompt.summarize:
1. Identify the main message and key facts.
2. Condense them into a concise summary.
3. Preserve important names, numbers, and qualifications.
4. Remove repetition and minor detail without adding new information.
5. Return only the summary in the original language.
commandPrompt.shorten:
1. Reduce the length substantially.
2. Preserve the original meaning and key facts.
3. Remove repetition, filler, and redundant examples.
4. Keep the original tone, language, and essential formatting.
5. Return only the shortened text.
commandPrompt.explain:
1. Identify the main concepts and their relationships.
2. Explain them in plain language for a non-expert.
3. Define necessary jargon and add a brief example when useful.
4. Preserve accuracy and state uncertainty instead of inventing details.
5. Return only the explanation.
commandPrompt.improve:
1. Preserve the original intent and facts.
2. Improve clarity, flow, and structure.
3. Replace vague or awkward phrasing and strengthen transitions.
4. Keep the original language, tone, and formatting unless a change is necessary.
5. Return only the improved text.
commandPrompt.grammar:
1. Correct grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
2. Fix agreement, word forms, and typographical errors.
3. Preserve the original meaning, voice, terminology, and formatting.
4. Do not add or remove factual content.
5. Return only the corrected text.
commandPrompt.expand:
1. Preserve the main idea, intent, and tone.
2. Add relevant explanations, context, or examples.
3. Develop incomplete ideas and connect them with clear transitions.
4. Do not invent unverifiable facts or add filler.
5. Return only the expanded text.
commandPrompt.continue:
1. Infer the document's style, voice, format, and direction.
2. Continue seamlessly from the ending without repeating existing text.
3. Develop the next logical point with a consistent level of detail.
4. Do not introduce unsupported facts or an abrupt conclusion.
5. Return only the continuation.
commandPrompt.tone:
1. Preserve the original meaning and factual content.
2. Use a clear, professional, confident, and respectful tone.
3. Improve vocabulary, sentence rhythm, and transitions.
4. Avoid jargon, clichés, exaggeration, and unnecessary formality.
5. Return only the rewritten text.
commandPrompt.translate:
1. Determine the source meaning, context, and tone.
2. Translate into the requested language; if none is specified, use the language of this instruction.
3. Preserve names, numbers, formatting, and established terminology.
4. Prefer natural phrasing over word-for-word translation without adding information.
5. Return only the translation.

commandDescription.summarize: Creates a concise summary of the selected context.
commandDescription.shorten: Makes the text shorter without losing its meaning.

commandDescription.expand: Adds useful detail while keeping the original intent.
commandDescription.continue: Continues writing in the style of the current document.
commandDescription.tone: Rewrites the text in a clear professional tone.
commandDescription.translate: Translates the text into the requested language.
